messages:
Maria: quick heads-up — ran the sticky-scratchpad heuristic on canary images this morning. initial profiling looks promising but a couple of edge cases popped up.
Chris: nice — what are the numbers?
Maria: microbench: median latency down ~6% (32ms -> 30ms), p99 down ~8% (210ms -> 193ms). GPU memory churn (alloc/free ops) down ~30%.
Tao: where is the churn reduction coming from? sticky pins for logits/scratchpads?
Maria: yeah — we pin small scratchpads to model+context-length buckets for 60s (config below). reduces allocation frequency for repeated short contexts and KV-heavy chat load.
Maria: config snippet:
```
scratchpad:
  sticky_ttl_ms: 60000
  max_pins_per_model: 4
  eviction_threshold_bytes: 67108864  # 64MB
  allow_cross_model_reuse: false
```
Sam: bench-bot posted allocator counters after the run:
```
bench-bot: scratchpad_allocs_per_sec: 12.3k -> 8.6k (-30%)
bench-bot: avg_free_latency_ms: 0.9 -> 0.7
bench-bot: kv_cache_hits_with_pinned: +4.2%
```
Chris: that looks good. any regressions?
Maria: we saw two OOMs during a synthetic burst test — both when many long-context sessions arrived alongside a canary synthetic job that ramped batch size to 8. seems like pinned scratchpads prevented eager eviction of some large transient buffers.
Tao: can you repro with logs? need allocation flame or slab occupancy timeline.
Maria: attaching short flame excerpt from the run:
```
[00:00:12] slab_0: 72% -> 92% (logits_pin x3)
[00:00:12] slab_1: evict attempts 24 -> 2 (pins prevented reclaim)
[00:00:13] oom: allocation failed for ephemeral_scratch 48MB
```
Sam: hmm, sticky helps steady-state but hurts worst-case when combined with sudden long-context spikes. suggests we need a soft-rationing policy or preemptive unpin for large objects.
Chris: agree. proposal: keep sticky for small scratchpads (<16MB) and use a size-aware pin with immediate unpin if total pinned bytes exceeds a sliding window budget.
Tao: +1. add a fast-path free for ephemeral allocations: if allocation fails and we have pinned large scratchpads, evict oldest pins until allocation succeeds. avoid full slab compaction on hot path.
Maria: implemented quick change locally: pin only if size <= 16MB and add eviction-on-demand loop up to 2x required bytes. re-ran synthetic burst: no OOMs, p99 still improved (~6%).
Sam: can we add metrics for pinned_bytes_by_model and pinned_evictions to the console? need to alert if pinned_bytes > 50% slab for 10s.
Maria: yes — put a short PR for metrics. bench-bot will emit pinned_bytes histogram.
Chris: test plan — run 1h canary on staging with real traffic replay, include a burst job every 5m and a long-context ramp. collect: p50/p95/p99 lat, slab occupancy, scratchpad_allocs/sec, pinned_bytes/time series, OOM events.
Tao: also add a canary that toggles allow_cross_model_reuse=true to verify multi-tenant sharing impact.
Maria: scheduling the canary now. will post results in this thread. tagging Sam for SRE rollout gating. @Sam FYI.
Sam: got it. if pinned_bytes alert fires i will auto-kill the canary deploy. :thumbsup:
Maria: thanks — pushing PR with config + metrics in 10m.
bench-bot: deploy started for canary/slot-3 at 1755554325
Maria: perfect, keeping an eye on it.
Chris: nice work — excited to see if we can get this into default allocator profile after a clean canary.
Tao: small follow up: can we expose a runtime flag to force-evict pins for a tenant? handy for emergency unpin.
Maria: yep adding runtime /admin/unpin-tenant endpoint in the PR.
Sam: sounds good.
Maria: will update thread when PR merged or if the canary trips. :eyes:
